children.value: is true, the values of the test statistic follow a standard normal distribution (i.e., the sampling distribution of the test statistic when the null hypothesis is true is N(0,1)). Therefore, p-values correspond to areas (probabilities) under the standard normal curve.

, p-values are found using the sampling distribution of the test statistic when the null hypothesis is true (also known as the “null distribution” of the test statistic). In this case, it was relatively easy to argue that the null distribution of our test statistic is N(0,1). As we’ll see, in other tests, other distributions come up (like the t-distribution and the F-distribution), which we will just mention briefly, and rely heavily on the output of our statistical package for obtaining the p-values.

With respect to the z-test for the population proportion: steps 1, 2, and 3 are completed; step 4 is what we will work on next.

In 2007, a Gallup poll estimated that 45% of U.S. adults rated their financial situation as “good.” We want to know if the proportion is smaller this year. We gather a random sample of 100 U.S. adults this year and find that 39 rate their financial situation as “good.” Statistical software gives the following output:

model.question: According to the output, what is the value of the test statistic, and what does it mean?

choices.text: z = −1.21—the sample proportion is 1.21 standard deviations below 0.45
choices.feedback: Correct! z = −1.21: the sample proportion 0.39 is 1.21 standard deviations below the null value 0.45.

choices.text: z = 0.114—the sample proportion is 0.114 standard deviations below 0.45
choices.feedback: 0.114 is the p-value, not the test statistic.

choices.text: z = 0.39—the sample proportion is 0.39 standard deviations below 0.45
choices.feedback: 0.39 is the sample proportion; the test statistic is its standardized (z) score.

model.hint: Find the Z-Value in the output.

model.question: Which statement correctly interprets the p-value of 0.114?

choices.text: If p were 0.45, the probability of a sample proportion of 0.39 or lower would be 0.114
choices.feedback: Correct! If the true proportion were still 0.45, there would be a 0.114 probability of getting a sample proportion of 0.39 or lower in a sample of 100.

choices.text: There is a 0.114 probability that the proportion is still 0.45
choices.feedback: The p-value is not the probability that H₀ is true.

choices.text: If p were 0.45, the probability of a sample proportion at least 0.06 away from 0.45 in either direction would be 0.114
choices.feedback: This describes a two-tailed calculation; the alternative here is one-sided (less than).

model.hint: The alternative is p < 0.45, so "extreme" means small.

model.question: Using α = 0.05, what is the correct conclusion?

choices.text: Do not reject H₀—there is not enough evidence that the proportion rating their situation "good" has decreased
choices.feedback: Correct! Since 0.114 > 0.05, the data do not provide enough evidence to conclude that the proportion has decreased.

choices.text: Reject H₀ and conclude the proportion has decreased
choices.feedback: 0.114 is LARGER than 0.05, so we cannot reject H₀.

choices.text: Accept H₀ and conclude the proportion is still 0.45
choices.feedback: Failing to reject H₀ does not prove the proportion is still 0.45.

children.value: The trustees of a local school district commission a survey to determine voter opinions about a possible bond measure to fund school upgrades. In a poll of 293 of the district’s 5,019 registered voters, 178 would support the bond measure. A hypothesis test was conducted to determine if such a bond would pass with the required 55% of the vote. Statistical software gives the following output:

model.question: Using α = 0.05, what should the trustees conclude?

choices.text: Reject H₀—there is significant evidence that support exceeds 55%, so the bond is likely to pass
choices.feedback: Correct! Since 0.024 < 0.05, the data provide significant evidence that more than 55% of registered voters support the measure—suggesting the bond would pass.

choices.text: Do not reject H₀—the evidence is not strong enough
choices.feedback: 0.024 is smaller than 0.05, so the result IS statistically significant.

choices.text: Reject H₀ (nothing further can be said)
choices.feedback: The conclusion needs context: rejecting H₀ here means support exceeds the required 55%.

model.hint: The p-value is 0.024. What does rejecting H₀ mean in context?

children.value: Do zinc supplements reduce a child’s risk of catching a cold? A medical study reports a p-value of 0.03.

model.question: Which of the following are valid interpretations of the p-value of 0.03? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: If zinc had no effect, results like those observed would occur with probability 0.03
choices.feedback: Valid! This is exactly what the p-value measures—the chance of results like these if zinc had no effect.

choices.text: The results are statistically significant at the 0.05 level
choices.feedback: Valid! Since 0.03 < 0.05, the results are statistically significant at the 0.05 level.

choices.text: There is a 3% chance that zinc has no effect on colds
choices.feedback: Invalid—the p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.text: Zinc reduces the risk of colds by 3%
choices.feedback: Invalid—the p-value says nothing about the size of the effect, only the strength of evidence that some effect exists.

model.hint: The p-value is a probability about the DATA computed assuming the null hypothesis (zinc has no effect) is true.
